newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ coalition talks resume with informal meetings.
newsitem.headline: NZ coalition talks resume with informal meetings.

text.p: Informal coalition talks aimed at establishing the shape of the next government resumed on Monday, with three more rounds of formal sessions set down for later in the week.
Informal sessions were held on Monday between nationalist NZ First and both the conservative National Party and the centre- left Labour Party as talks entered their sixth week.
An agreement is expected to be announced either late this week or early next week.
NZ First has 17 MPs and holds the balance of power after the October 12 election. Parliament must reconvene no later than December 13.

National has 44 seats and could form a majority coalition government with NZ First in the 120 seat parliament. Labour has 37 seats and would need the tacit support of the 13 left-wing Alliance MPs to form a government with NZ First.
Party sources said small groups of NZ First, Labour and National MPs are focusing on specific policy areas, but major decisions are reserved for formal talks.
"Formal talks may start up again this week depending on progress," a spokesman for NZ First leader Winston Peters said.
A spokesman for National caretaker Prime Minister Jim Bolger said formal talks with NZ First were set down for 2 p.m. on Tuesday and 10 a.m. on Wednesday and Thursday.

National has cancelled its regular caucus meeting on Tuesday and the next full caucus meeting would be held on Tuesday December 3. It was possible one could be held on Thursday if a deal was close, Bolger's spokesman said.
A spokesman for Labour leader Helen Clark said a session of formal talks with NZ First had been set down for Tuesday at 5 p.m. but the meeting had not been confirmed.

Labour will hold its regular caucus meeting on Tuesday at which it will discuss progress in the coalition talks and be briefed on the Taranaki land claim -- the largest outstanding Maori land claim facing the incoming government.
The incumbent National government has reached a settlement on fisheries claims and last year settled the large Waikato Tainui land claim in the North Island.
The South Island Ngai Tahu claim has been settled in principle but must be ratified by the incoming government.
All five Maori electorates returned NZ First MPs at the election and the treatment of issues important to Maori is seen as an important component in any coalition deal.

NZ First leader Winston Peters has said agreements with both Labour and National will be referred to the NZ First caucus of MPs before a final decision is made on which party it will support to form a government.
